data.title: Lignocaine + Prilocaine (EMLA cream/gel)
data.summary: XI Miscellaneous · Eutectic mixture of local anaesthetics (lidocaine 2.5% + prilocaine 2.5%)
data.body:
_Topicals · XI Miscellaneous_

**Class:** Eutectic mixture of local anaesthetics (lidocaine 2.5% + prilocaine 2.5%)

## Mechanism of action
- The two amides mixed in equal amounts have a melting point below room temperature (eutectic) → a liquid oil that penetrates intact skin
- Blocks voltage-gated sodium channels in dermal nerve endings → surface anaesthesia

## Indications in dermatology & STI
- Topical anaesthesia before venepuncture, IV cannulation, laser treatments, curettage of molluscum, wart removal, superficial biopsies, split-skin grafts, microneedling, leg ulcer debridement
- Genital mucosa (shorter application time: 5–10 min)

## Dose & formulations
- Apply a thick layer (1–2 g per 10 cm²) under occlusion (film dressing) for 60 min (depth about 3 mm); 120 min for deeper anaesthesia (about 5 mm)
- Infant limits: 0–3 months — max 1 g over 10 cm² for 1 h; 3–12 months — max 2 g over 20 cm²; larger limits in older children by weight
- Wipe off before the procedure

## Adverse effects
- Blanching then redness at application site (vasoconstriction followed by vasodilation)
- Methaemoglobinaemia — the most serious adverse effect (prilocaine metabolite o-toluidine oxidises haemoglobin); risk in infants under 3 months, large areas, G6PD deficiency, with other oxidising drugs
- Purpura, contact urticaria, irritant reactions
- Eye injury if applied near eyes (corneal abrasion)

## Contraindications
- Congenital or idiopathic methaemoglobinaemia
- Infants under 12 months on methaemoglobin-inducing drugs; premature infants (under 37 weeks)
- Amide anaesthetic allergy; open wounds (except leg ulcers per protocol); near eyes or middle ear

## Drug interactions
- Methaemoglobin-inducing drugs: dapsone, sulfonamides, nitrates (nitroglycerin), paracetamol (high dose), phenytoin, antimalarials (primaquine, chloroquine)
- Class I antiarrhythmics: additive toxicity

## Monitoring
- In infants or large areas: watch for cyanosis (grey-blue colour with normal oxygen); treat methaemoglobinaemia with methylene blue (avoid in G6PD deficiency)

## Pregnancy & lactation
Safe in pregnancy (old FDA category B).

## Viva points
- Eutectic = mixture melts below room temperature → penetrates intact skin
- 60 min under occlusion
- Methaemoglobinaemia due to prilocaine (worse with dapsone)

_Sources: Wolverton 4e ch.58 (Local anesthetics — EMLA, methemoglobinemia); Khopkar (Miscellaneous agents). Facts summarised in our own words; Wolverton followed where books differ._
